summary: Shu-fen Chen is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at National Tsing Hua University, where she later held a professorship attested in 2010. She studied under Chin-Fa Lien and completed doctoral work under Hans Henrich Hock.
Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who served as a professor at Karnatak University, attested in 2001, and in the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore, attested in 2002.

Shudo Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata. He spent his career at Komazawa University, progressing from assistant in 1971 to professor in 1984, and served as acting head of Matsugaoka Bunko.

Shuhong Chang (1904–1994) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. After studying in Lyon and Paris, he taught at the Central Academy of Fine Arts and served as director and honorary director of the Dunhuang Academy.

Shuichi Kato (1919–2008) worked in Japanology, history, and philosophy after medical studies at the University of Tokyo. He taught at Sophia University, Free University of Berlin, and UBC, and later directed the Kyoto Museum for World Peace at Ritsumeikan University.

Shuichi Maida (1906–1967) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University from roughly 1928 to 1931 and studied under Haya Akegarasu between approximately 1930 and 1954.

Shuichi Nara (born 1961) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Keio University. His posts include researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and lecturer at Chuo University, attested in 2026.

Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies researcher who held posts as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and researcher at Bukkyo University (attested 2003), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2006), and Musashino University (attested 2006).

Shujiro Shimada (1907–1994) was a scholar of Japanology, sinology, and art history who studied at Kyoto University from roughly 1928 to 1931 and held a post at Princeton University from around 1962 to 1975.

Shujun Motegi (born 1951) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and at Kyoto University. He later served as a professor of ethics at Shinshu University, attested in 2010.

Shuken Ito (born 1947) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at Komazawa University. He held academic posts there from 1973 onward, becoming a professor in 1991, and visited Aichi Gakuin University in 1998.
Shuman Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Northwestern University under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn, and also studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi.

Shuming Liang (1893–1988) was a philosopher, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Shuntian Middle School. He joined the philosophy department at Peking University in 1917 and founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and China Democratic League.

Shumpei Ueyama (1921–2012) was a philosopher and historian educated at Kyoto University, where he later served as professor from 1968. He also served as president of Kyoto City University of Arts and director of the Kyoto National Museum.
Shun Hidaka is a Buddhist studies researcher who served as an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University, attested in 2014.

Shun'ei Hirai (born 1930) is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He spent his career at Komazawa University, serving as professor, vice president in 1986, and later professor emeritus.

Shun'ei Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He held posts at Ryukoku University, attested in 1990, and as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College, attested in 1995.
Shunei Tsuboi (1923–2010) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Bukkyo University, attested in 1963 and 1972.

Shunji Hosaka (born 1956) is a religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Waseda University. He taught at Reitaku University (~1990–2001) and Chuo University (~2001–2021), and held lecturing posts attested in 2026.

Shunkyo Katsumata (1909–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1931–1934). He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University (~1946–1982), where he became professor emeritus.
